title: Applied ML evals: Prompt Sets, Quantization Profiles, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Aisha Rahman
body:
Overview:

This playbook describes Redwood's end-to-end processes and standards for prompt-set onboarding, benchmark selection, quantization profile evaluation, and regression triage using the Eval Harness. It consolidates procedures used by Applied ML, Model Onboarding, and SRE partners to ensure consistent quality guardrails and repeatable regression investigations.

Scope:
- All customer-visible prompt sets used in hosted APIs, Dedicated presets, and Private deployments.
- Benchmarks used for model selection, release gating, and continuous monitoring.
- Quantization profiles evaluated for production serving (int8 / q4 / q2-family).
- Regression triage flow for any automated detection flagged by the Eval Harness or observability pipelines.

Ownership and SLAs:
- Doc owner: Applied ML (owner_team: engineering).
- Primary contacts: Aisha Rahman (Applied ML lead), Marcus Lee (Eval Harness infra), Sofia Alvarez (Model Onboarding).
- Review cadence: Quarterly review and after any major model rollout (>10% traffic change).
- SLOs tied to evals: maintain stable prompt-set pass-rate >= 98% relative to baseline on critical prompt buckets; quantization-induced quality delta <= 1.5% absolute on curated metrics for targeted workloads.

Key Definitions:
- Prompt set: A curated collection of inputs plus expected outputs (gold labels or evaluation criteria) representing a user workload.
- Eval Harness: Our automated evaluation framework that runs prompt sets and computes metrics (BLEU, ROUGE, Exact Match, embedding-similarity, heuristic safety checks, hallucination detectors).
- Quantization profile: A named configuration describing quantization scheme (e.g. q8_onnx, q4_fused, int8_gpt) and allowed perf/quality bounds.
- Regression triage: The investigative workflow triggered when eval metrics degrade beyond configured thresholds.

Prompt-set onboarding (step-by-step):
1) Intake: create a new prompt-set issue in the Applied ML board. Include: owner, description, expected metrics, label taxonomy, and sample size.
2) Schema validation: prompts must include id, input, expected_output (if available), category tag, and complexity score (1-5). Use the following JSON schema snippet for validation: 

    {
      "type": "array",
      "items": { "type": "object", "properties": {"id": {"type": "string"}, "input": {"type": "string"}, "expected_output": {"type": "string"}, "category": {"type": "string"} }, "required": ["id", "input", "category"] }
    }

3) Quality review: two reviewers (Applied ML + Product) must approve the prompt semantics and label coverage. Add the prompt-set to the catalog once approved.
4) Baseline run: run the prompt-set against the current production model and at least two candidate models (including any quantized variants) via the Eval Harness. Store results in the eval-run artifact store and tag the run with build_id and model_version.

Benchmark selection and coverage guidelines:
- Benchmarks must cover these axes: intent diversity, length distribution, domain specificity, safety-sensitive examples, and adversarial cases.
- Minimum prompt-set sizes: small (100), medium (1k), large (10k) depending on gating level.
- Critical buckets: authentication flows, billing/account management, code-completion, and safety-sensitive queries.
- Metric matrix: define primary metric per bucket (e.g., exact-match for structured outputs, embedding-similarity for semantic search, ROUGE for summarization).

Quantization profile evaluation:
- For each quantization profile under consideration, run the following steps:
  1) Functional correctness checks (smoke tests): 100 samples across critical buckets.
  2) Statistical regression test: run medium-sized prompt-sets and compute per-bucket delta vs baseline (float32).
  3) Latency and throughput profiling: measure p50/p95 latency and tokens/sec under the workload used by the target route.
  4) Memory and stability: monitor OOMs, process restarts, and KV-cache correctness for long-context runs.
- Pass criteria: per-bucket metric delta <= configured threshold (default 1.5% absolute) AND p95 latency within 1.2x of baseline unless explicitly allowed in the quantization waiver.
- Recording: attach quantization profile metadata to the model_version in the model catalog. Include kernel hints and any split-layer exceptions.

Integration with the Eval Harness:
- Eval runs are defined by a YAML job config that references: model_version, prompt_set_id, num_shards, metrics, and post-processing hooks. Example CLI:

    ri-eval run --config=examples/medium-eval.yaml --model=redwood-gpt-13b-v2 --profile=q4_fused --tag=2026-11-15

- Required outputs from every eval run: run_id, start/end timestamps, artifacts (raw responses), metrics.json (per-bucket), and a triage summary if any thresholds are violated.
- Artifact retention: default 90 days for large runs, 365 days for release gating runs.

Automated regression detection (alerts):
- Alert triggers: any per-bucket metric delta > threshold (default 1.5% absolute) OR safety metric fails (any unsafe classification increase > 0.5%).
- Alert routing: Alerts post to #applied-ml-regressions Slack channel and create a ticket in the Regression Triage board. Pager escalation only if production traffic > 100k requests/day and degradation affects critical buckets.

Regression triage playbook (on alert):
1) Triage lead assignment (within 30 minutes): the oncall Applied ML engineer picks up the ticket.
2) Immediate mitigation: if rollback criteria met (see rollback checklist below), coordinate with Release Engineering to initiate a model rollback and enable fallback routing to baseline model.
3) Investigation steps:
   a) Reproduce: re-run the Eval Harness on the latest production snapshot and the previous known-good snapshot.
   b) Narrow: run differences by bucket and by prompt sub-slice (use the harness' shard-runner to isolate failing cases).
   c) Hypothesize: check for changes in tokenization, model_version, quantization profile, preprocessing transforms, and post-processing regexes.
   d) Validate: run controlled A/B experiments if the root cause is unclear and rollback is not immediate.
4) Root cause classification: label the ticket with one of {model-quality, quantization, preproc, postproc, data-drift, harness-bug, infra}.
5) Resolution and rollback checklist:
   - Confirm rollback criteria (e.g., >2% absolute loss on critical bucket OR safety regression).
   - Prepare rollback plan: model_version, route rules, monitoring windows.
   - Execute rollback during low-impact window when possible; notify customers per SLA if rolling back customer-dedicated models.
   - Post-rollback verify: run focused evals and monitor production metrics for 24 hours.

Postmortem and preventive actions:
- For all gated regressions, create a postmortem within 3 business days capturing timeline, root cause, and action items.
- Recommended preventive controls: expand prompt-set coverage, add pre-release quantization smoke tests in CI, and increase eval-run cadence for high-risk routes.

Runbook snippets and useful commands:
- Run a quick smoke eval against production model:
    ri-eval run --model=prod-latest --prompt-set=critical-authentication --samples=200 --output=./artifacts/quick-smoke
- Compare two runs and generate triage summary:
    ri-eval compare --run-a=20261114-01 --run-b=20261113-08 --out=triage-summary.json

Appendix: Example eval YAML (medium-eval.yaml)

    job_name: medium-regression-check
    model_version: redwood-gpt-13b-v2
    prompt_set_id: sec-critical-1k
    shards: 8
    metrics:
      - name: exact_match
        target_bucket: auth
      - name: embedding_similarity
        target_bucket: semantic-search
    postprocessors:
      - name: normalize-whitespace

Notes and references:
- Related pages: model onboarding playbook, quantization profiles best practices, eval-harness developer guide.
- Contact Applied ML on #applied-ml for onboarding assistance or to request new prompt-set categories.

This playbook is intended to be a single source of truth for teams running or responding to eval-driven regressions. Keep it updated with concrete examples and link to run artifacts for future investigations.
